text:
A: Hiya mate, how you doing? Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, I can hear you fine. Darren.
A: Craig. Nice one. Where you based, Darren?
B: Halesowen. West Midlands, Black Country, sort of.
A: Lovely. I'm Cottingham, just outside Hull. How's your day been? I've just come off a run of nights so I'm a bit knackered, but fine, do you know what I mean.
B: Nights... what's that, factory?
A: Chemical plant, out at Saltend, east of Hull. I'm a process operator, so control room, plant rounds, twelve-hour shifts, days and nights. It's alright, to be fair. Long blocks off as well, which is the best bit. What about you?
B: Garden centre. Part time, Saturdays mostly. Tills and the outdoor plants. I do the school runs and that the rest of the week, my wife's on hospital shifts.
A: Ah, so you get shifts as well, just second hand. Kids?
B: Two. Fifteen and eleven. The fifteen-year-old's hard work at the minute, to be honest.
A: Fifteen, I can imagine. I was a nightmare at fifteen, my mum'll tell you. Saw your kitchen on the photo, spice rack absolutely rammed. You a cook, then?
B: Curries, mostly. From scratch. Neighbour showed me how a few years back and I've been at it since. Grow my own chillies in a little greenhouse.
A: See, I do a curry from a jar and tart it up a bit. Bit of extra garlic, chuck some chillies in, and I tell everyone it's homemade. Rachel, the wife, she knows. She does all the proper cooking. But it's her busy season at work, she's an accountant, so I'm doing most of the teas at the minute. Have you ever had a pattie? Hull thing. Pattie and chips.
B: No. What is it?
A: Right, so, it's mashed potato and sage, made into a sort of patty, battered and deep-fried at the chippy. Sounds daft, but honestly, with chips and a bit of gravy, it's unbelievable. Anyone from outside Hull, I make them have one. My mate from Leeds, he said it was just a potato in batter, and I said, mate, it's a way of life. Sorry, I've gone off on one there.
B: No, you're alright. Sounds like something my lad'd eat.
A: He would, mate. What do you do for fun, when you're not cooking?
B: What do I do... er, walk, mostly. Canal towpaths, up Clent Hills. Read a lot. Local history, canals, the chain-making. My dad worked the chain works, so.
A: Oh, that's proper. Hull's same with the docks. My dad was on the docks, then drove wagons. You into sport?
B: Wolves. Only get to Molineux once or twice a season now, the price of it. Used to do five-a-side till my knees went.
A: Knees! Same, mate. Played rugby league till my late twenties, knee went, that was that. I still do five-a-side Wednesdays if shifts let me, but I'm not quick. Hull FC, I'm a season ticket holder. Do you get much rugby league down your way?
B: Not really, no. Bit of union. I'd watch it if it were on, to be fair.
A: You need to come up for a game. Honestly, best atmosphere going. I'll get you a pattie as well.
B: Two for one, then.
